rationale: Classification: definite execution, no exception. Python 3.14 static reasoning; no execution. Inside `make`, the nested `def inner` binds `inner` as a local of make, so the `inner` in `functools.partial(inner, ...)` is that local function, not the module-level `inner`. `functools.partial` stores `func` and the positional args tuple at construction. Calling the returned partial with no arguments therefore calls the local `inner(["pacman", "-S", "r22-cxlocal"])`, which reaches `subprocess.run` with that literal argv. Exactly one observed host_mutation row, zero unparsed. The module-level `inner` is never called, so `pacman -Q r22-cxlocal-module` never runs. This attacks returned-partial identity resolution that looks up the wrapped name in module bindings instead of factory-local bindings at the return. Limits: this is exact static semantics for this text, not current-code behavior. With the module-level decoy removed, a resolver that misses the local def would be silent; that variant is not frozen here.
